title: The ideal of a regular local quotient is generated by parameters
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] of dimension $d$, and let $I\subsetneq R$ be an ideal such that $R/I$ is a regular local ring as well. Then there exist $x_1,\ldots,x_d\in\mathfrak m$ generating $\mathfrak m$ (a regular system of parameters) and an integer $0\le c\le d$ such that $I=(x_1,\ldots,x_c)$.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 00NR, lemma-regular-quotient-regular, statement (line 25750 in the source read).

proof.text: Because $I$ is proper and $R$ is local, $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-quotient-independent-generators] to obtain a finite set $s\subseteq\mathfrak m$ whose ideal span is $I$ and whose images are linearly independent in $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ over $\kappa$.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 00NR (lemma-regular-quotient-regular), proof setup and the choice of independent elements (lines 25758-25770 in the source read).

proof.text: Let $c=|s|$ and enumerate $s$ as $x_1,\ldots,x_c$. The cotangent space has dimension $d$ because $R$ is regular local [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-cotangent-dimension], so the independent classes of the $x_i$ extend to a basis by choosing lifts $x_{c+1},\ldots,x_d\in\mathfrak m$. Their classes span $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$; Nakayama [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] therefore gives that $x_1,\ldots,x_d$ generate $\mathfrak m$. Thus they are a regular system of parameters and $0\le c\le d$.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 00NR (lemma-regular-quotient-regular), proof: supplement independent classes to a minimal system of generators and use Nakayama (lines 25767-25771).

proof.text: The first $c$ elements are exactly the enumeration of $s$, and the ideal span of $s$ is $I$ by step 1. Hence $I=(x_1,\ldots,x_c)$, while step 2 gives the required generation of $\mathfrak m$ and the bound $c\le d$.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 00NR (lemma-regular-quotient-regular), conclusion identifying the chosen generators of I (lines 25767-25774).
